_note: A routing option is one (model, effort) pair. Variant id is '<model id>@<effort>'. Prices are USD per 1M tokens.

xhigh.description: long deliberation for genuinely hard problems

max.description: maximum reasoning compute; slowest and dearest

models.description: Cheapest GPT 5-6 tier at $0.20/$1.20 per 1M tokens, 1/25th of Sol on input. Holds ~85% of Sol's quality on short tasks: Terminal-Bench 2.1 84.7 vs Sol's 88.8, Agents' Last Exam 50.3 vs 53.6.
models.jev_role: High-volume Jev preset calls. Tool-guard and completion checks on every agent step, where per-call cost dominates and the decision is usually clear-cut.
avoid_when: long context: MRCR recall is 41.3 against Terra's 89.6, so the 1.05M window is not usable in practice

models.description: The GPT 5-6 default. Lands within 2-3 points of Sol on most benchmarks at under half the price: Terminal-Bench 2.1 87.4 vs 88.8, Agents' Last Exam 50.4 vs 53.6, MRCR long-context recall 89.6 vs 91.5. $2/$12 per 1M.
models.jev_role: Default worker once Jev returns proceed_fast. The bulk of cleared agent turns, and the right choice for long-context work that does not need frontier reasoning.

models.description: GPT 5-6 flagship and the only tier with max reasoning effort and Ultra mode. Leads its family on long-horizon agentic work (Agents' Last Exam 53.6), web navigation (BrowseComp 92.2) and computer use (OSWorld 2.0 62.6). $5/$30 per 1M.
models.jev_role: Escalation target for deep_review or split_task, especially browser-driven or computer-use work where it beats the Claude line. For repo-level coding, prefer Opus 5.
avoid_when: repo-level coding: SWE-bench Pro 64.6 against Opus 5's 79.2

models.description: Strongest coding model available here: SWE-bench Verified 96.0 and Pro 79.2, against Sol's Pro 64.6 and Sonnet 5's 63.2. Also leads abstract reasoning by a wide margin, ARC-AGI-3 30.2 where the next best scores 7.8. Extended thinking on by default. $5/$25 per 1M, same input price as Sol.
models.jev_role: Escalation target for deep_review, block, or tool-guard review. The model to hold the plan on a hard refactor while cheaper variants execute its steps.
strengths: catching its own errors before reporting done
avoid_when: per-step routing decisions a fast variant can serve

models.description: Best coding value here: SWE-bench Verified 85.2 at $2/$10 per 1M, matching Terra's price while beating it on repo-level work. Terminal-Bench 2.0 80.4 beat Opus 4.8's 74.6, the first time a Sonnet passed its Opus sibling on a major coding benchmark.
models.jev_role: Default worker for cleared agent turns. Medium-stakes work needing real code comprehension but not frontier deliberation.
avoid_when: genuinely ambiguous work at high stakes
problems where ARC-AGI-class reasoning is the bottleneck

models.description: Fastest option here at ~89 tokens/sec, 2x quicker to respond than Sonnet 4. SWE-bench Verified 73.3 beats Luna's tier on code while costing more ($1/$5 vs $0.20/$1.20). Smallest context of any model here at 200K.
models.jev_role: Per-step Jev preset calls and mechanical edits where the work is code-shaped. Pick Luna instead when the task is not code and cost dominates.
avoid_when: context above 200K: the smallest window here by 5x

thresholds._note: Difficulty (0-3, from the Jev assessment) sets a capability floor. min_tier always applies. 'require' gates on a published benchmark and is skipped for models that do not publish it — unknown is not failure, because no code benchmark spans both model families. min_effort raises the deliberation floor with difficulty, so a hard task cannot be served at a glance. 'require_published' names metrics a model must actually report to qualify; use it only for a kind with a specialist benchmark, where silence really is evidence of absence.

_long_context.why: a large window is not usable context; Luna scores 41.3 against Terra's 89.6
